xmldoc.short_description: Debug Nelson files from an editor over the Debug Adapter Protocol.

description.p: The advanced command line started with --dap drives the interpreter over its standard input and output as a Debug Adapter Protocol channel. An editor that speaks this protocol launches the process, sets breakpoints, runs a file and steps through it, using the same engine debugger as dbstop, dbstep and dbcont.
The channel is headless: figures render without a window and no prompt or banner is printed, so the output carries protocol frames only.

Supported features are breakpoints, conditional breakpoints, step in, step over, step out, continue, pause, the call stack, the local variables of the current scope, expression evaluation for the watch list and for data tips, and stops on caught or uncaught errors.

The option --dap-port adds a Debug Adapter channel to a notebook kernel started with --notebook-kernel. The kernel listens on the given port on the loopback interface (127.0.0.1) and serves the protocol over a TCP socket, while the notebook cells keep running on the standard input and output channel. An editor attaches to the port to debug a cell against the same live interpreter the kernel already drives, so the breakpoints, the call stack and the variables reflect the running session.

The debug channel reconnects: when the editor detaches, the kernel clears the debug breakpoints, resumes any paused cell and keeps serving, and a later attach reuses the same port. The port value is a number between 1 and 65535.
This mode is used by the Nelson extension for Visual Studio Code to provide its debugging user interface; the mode itself is editor independent.

example_item.example_item_description: Set a breakpoint, then start the file from the editor debugger.
